title: Uncle teaches him to read; Johnny Dodds lends an E-flat clarinet
summary: His uncle taught him to read music and divide bars, not fingering; Dodds, who played in the uncle's band, lent a little E-flat clarinet that small fingers could manage.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: You mentioned that your uncle taught you music, your --
Was he the one who taught you the clarinet fingering?

You see, he taught me how to read the music and the division of the bars and all that. I had a book, you see. And he taught me that. Then when he found out that I could do pretty well like that, they didn't give me a clarinet at all to start with, which I am very happy until this day, you know, because that would have been double -- you know, like, too much for my little brain to manipulate, trying to read the music, and the fingering of the clarinet. And then my hands were so small, and so they used an E-flat, what they call an E-flat clarinet, to play parades with, the brass band, because they're shrill. They can make a lot of noise, you know.

And so the guy that played in his band was Johnny Dodds. He played clarinet in his band, and he had one, so my uncle borrowed his E-flat. Yeah, so he borrowed -- he loaned my uncle his little E-flat clarinet since he wasn't playing in many parades. And only I'd give it back to him when he had a parade to play.
